scope: Public curriculum, lesson, scenario and tutorial audit for Ascend Local to Internet / practical Internet services operations.
methods: Retrieved first-party public HTML with Python urllib; retained response SHA-256 and metadata.
Inspected public source text; for four DigitalOcean tutorials also loaded the pages in isolated Chromium and read the rendered article bodies.
Attempted Chromium access to Cisco Networking Basics; only the title/navigation was available in the sampled session.
No accounts created, courses purchased, external lab sessions started, infrastructure provisioned, or messages sent.

sources.title: Free Computer Networking Course by Cisco: Start Learning Now
sources.evidence_status: limited course metadata and navigation only
supports: The official route and title advertising a free Networking Basics course were retrieved.
limitations: The initial response contained a JavaScript shell.
The Chromium visit rendered navigation but no substantive course text.
No course outline, Packet Tracer exercises, hardware alternative, download entitlement, or assessment claim is supported by this retrieval.

rendered_document.title: Free Computer Networking Course by Cisco: Start Learning Now

sources.title: Initial Server Setup with Ubuntu | DigitalOcean
supports: The tutorial configures a new server with a non-root sudo user, SSH keys, and a firewall.
It requires validating the new account and SSH access before closing the original session.
The article describes applicability to cloud VMs, VPS, and bare-metal servers.
limitations: Commands were not run in this audit.
The requested Ubuntu 22.04 URL redirects to a generic Ubuntu guide; use recorded versions and reference tests rather than assuming all future releases.
The initial HTML text extraction did not expose the article body; the substantive review used rendered text.

rendered_document.title: Initial Server Setup with Ubuntu | DigitalOcean

sources.title: How To Set Up WireGuard on Ubuntu 22.04 | DigitalOcean
supports: The tutorial configures a WireGuard server and peer, IPv4/IPv6 address ranges, keys, network/firewall behaviour, and optional Internet gateway routing.
The client may be the learner's local machine, a remote server, or a mobile device.
The page explicitly cautions that provider bandwidth overages can cost money.
limitations: No VPN, route, or firewall was configured.
A named Ubuntu-version tutorial needs reference testing on the chosen guest/host versions.
The article body was reviewed after Chromium rendering.

rendered_document.title: How To Set Up WireGuard on Ubuntu 22.04 | DigitalOcean

sources.title: An Introduction to HAProxy and Load Balancing Concepts | DigitalOcean
supports: The article describes HAProxy frontends/backends, L4/L7 routing, balancing algorithms, sticky sessions, health checks, and HA.
It identifies a single load balancer as a possible single point of failure even when backends are redundant.
limitations: The examples were not executed or benchmarked.
A conceptual load-balancing article does not establish a complete concurrency/capacity curriculum.
The article body was reviewed after Chromium rendering.

rendered_document.title: An Introduction to HAProxy and Load Balancing Concepts | DigitalOcean

sources.title: How To Install and Configure Postfix on Ubuntu | DigitalOcean
supports: The article teaches foundational Postfix MTA setup and testing with a mail client.
It explicitly says the exercise yields bare-bones mail functionality, not a full-featured email server.
It discusses domain/DNS configuration and operational delivery complications.
limitations: No email was sent and no mail server deployed.
The tutorial alone cannot establish full mailbox service, reliable public deliverability, or safe long-term operation.
Specific technical/provider assertions need primary-product verification and reference tests.
The article body was reviewed after Chromium rendering.

rendered_document.title: How To Install and Configure Postfix on Ubuntu | DigitalOcean

sources.title: About Killercoda | Interactive Environments
supports: Interactive Linux/Kubernetes scenarios run in the browser.
The technology description explicitly identifies disposable VMs for interactive-environment isolation.
Free and paid membership have different finite session/concurrency/queue allowances.
limitations: No scenario was allocated.
Advertised usage counts and membership limits are provider statements at retrieval time.
This is not evidence that Ascend can safely host arbitrary administration work in its existing fixed container adapters.

sources.title: Creator Documentation | Killercoda
supports: Scenarios are authored in Git using JSON, Markdown, and scripts and synchronize on push.
An optional step verification script runs when CHECK is pressed and succeeds with exit code zero.
Scenario groups and differing environment images are documented.
limitations: No scenario was authored/published or run.
A step check alone does not establish independent assessment authority or complete tamper resistance.

sources.title: DevOps Roadmap & Learning Path | Kodekloud
supports: The path lists Linux, VirtualBox/Vagrant networking, IPs and ports, Apache, and SSL/TLS as prerequisites before scripting, Git, CI, containers, orchestration, IaC, and monitoring.
Topic and role paths and a hands-on readiness test are linked.
limitations: The readiness test and enrolled labs were not run.
The prerequisite topic names do not establish a complete hypervisor administration or multi-tenant VM-hosting curriculum.
Free offers in navigation do not establish free access to the complete path.

sources.title: Introduction to DevOps and Site Reliability Engineering (LFS162) - Linux Foundation - Education
supports: LFS162 covers DevOps/SRE, cloud, containers, IaC, CI/CD, and observability.
The prerequisite list includes intermediate Linux, networking, scripting, security, virtualization, and administration knowledge.
The reviewed page lists zero-price enrolment and a 4GB RAM/2vCPU minimum laptop configuration for this course.
limitations: The reviewer did not enrol or complete a lab.
Its minimum laptop specification is not a benchmark for Ascend's full track or VM-host workloads.
The public outline does not establish complete tunnel/mail or hypervisor administration practice.

sources.title: Linux Upskill Challenge - Linux Upskill Challenge
sources.evidence_status: public curriculum and lesson index inspected
supports: The course describes free/open learning material without a required subscription or registration.
Its Linux administration sequence includes SSH, packages, services, permissions, networking/firewalls, scheduling, file transfer, archiving, source builds, log rotation, and scripting.
limitations: No entire-course reference run was performed.
The source does not provide a measured microSD or full Ascend-track resource budget.

sources.title: Day 9 — Diving into networking — Linux Upskill Challenge
supports: The networking lesson inspects listeners, changes firewall reachability, tests the effect, and restores access while preserving SSH.
The lesson links independent SadServers troubleshooting cases after instruction.
limitations: No firewall was changed during this audit.
Ascend should refine broad exposure/security wording: all-interface binding alone does not establish public Internet reachability.
Published commands and illustrative outputs require version-specific reference testing before adoption.

sources.title: Best DevOps Bootcamp | TechWorld with Nana
sources.evidence_status: public syllabus and project descriptions inspected
supports: Build/package work is taught manually before later automation.
Projects combine CI, registries, Docker, cloud VMs, Kubernetes, IaC, observability, and application recovery.
The commercial page describes independent exercises and cloud costs in addition to course cost.
limitations: Paid classes and projects were not taken.
Marketing, salary, graduate-outcome, and production-grade claims were not independently validated.
Cloud credits and free-tier examples on the page need current provider validation before reuse.

sources.title: SadServers: Linux, DevOps & SRE Labs | Interview & Hiring Assessment
supports: The catalog covers Linux/networking/DNS/storage/SSH, web servers, databases, containers, infrastructure, and observability.
Scenario entries expose difficulty, time, access, task type, and a test when applicable.
The Saint John scenario requires stopping a log writer while retaining the log file; exploratory activities without scored checks also exist.
limitations: No VM scenario was started or solved.
Availability and entitlement vary by scenario.
Published checker descriptions do not independently prove the whole grading system or learner transfer.

sources.title: FAQ | SadServers
sources.evidence_status: public product and scenario FAQ inspected
supports: The platform documents real VMs, browser terminal access, clues, automated checks, and account progress.
Root access varies by scenario; direct SSH/CLI access is documented for eligible paid plans.
The FAQ describes inspecting/running a scenario check script and says modifying that script causes validation failure.
limitations: Account, paid-plan, direct-SSH, and checker behaviour were not exercised.
The documented tamper check was not independently audited.

sources.title: Day 0 — Get Your Own Server — Linux Upskill Challenge
supports: The guide explicitly allows local servers/VMs, WSL/VirtualBox, or other available hardware when cloud hosting is unsuitable.
The environment must support package updates/installation and remote SSH access; the source says most course commands work the same regardless of VM location.
A rented VPS is explained as a VM using part of a physical host.
limitations: No individual VM, VPS, or physical device was created.
Using a local VM does not automatically verify Internet routing or physical-device behaviour.
No complete VM-host administration, resizing, quota, or multi-user control plane is established by this guide.
This audit supports curriculum design and narrow claims about the inspected public material; it is not evidence that the reviewer completed the courses.
No claim of educational efficacy, independent skill transfer, job readiness, or production reliability is established by the providers' marketing or testimonials.
Coverage gaps mean not established in this selected sample, not an exhaustive claim that the platform has no such material.
HTTP 200 does not establish accessible course content; Cisco is deliberately marked metadata-only.
Current free-tier, pricing, account and hardware capabilities must be rechecked before learners rely on them.
Temporary retrieval files remained outside the repository; this ledger contains citations, hashes and paraphrased findings, not copied third-party lessons.
